items.content:
It wasn’t long ago that a Knicks vs. Timberwolves matchup almost felt like a mini-rivalry—one of the few the Knicks had against a team from the Western Conference.

Given the East Coast vs. West Coast of it all, and the LeBron vs. New York effect, the Lakers made for a fun matchup. The Spurs and Knicks have had some tough battles, including the 1999 Finals and the 2024 Christmas Day game, and that pseudo-rivalry was elevated to a new level with the 2026 Finals. But whenever the Knicks and Timberwolves played each other over the last two seasons, it felt like there was more on the line than just the game. It was a battle for narrative, not just bragging rights. Which team won the Karl-Anthony Towns trade? How would former Knicks Julius Randle and Donte DiVincenzo play against their former team? Now, with the Knicks having won a championship and Randle moving from Minnesota to Brooklyn, this matchup no longer feels as personal.

That doesn’t mean that it’ll be a bad game. Nor does it mean that the Timberwolves won’t be a tough opponent. At 11-4, they enter Thursday night with a better record than the Knicks despite being without star guard Anthony Edwards since he underwent knee surgery on October 29. And contrary to expectations, their success hasn’t been a result of LaMelo Ball putting up insane offensive numbers. Their scoring has been incredibly balanced, with Ayo Dosunmu averaging 18.6 PPG, Ball averaging 17.7 PPG, and Jaden McDaniels averaging 17.1 PPG. Even without a single player averaging more than 20 PPG, they’ve managed to have the 12th-highest offensive rating.

Where they’ve remained elite Edwards, though, is on the defensive end. The Timberwolves, thanks in large part to four-time Defensive Player of the Year winner Rudy Gobert, have been incredibly dominant defensively. As of today, they have the best defensive rating in the league at 104, two full points better than the second-place Celtics. They rank third in the league in opponents’ field goal percentage, first in opponents’ three-point percentage, and force the sixth-most turnovers per game.

The Knicks, who haven’t completely gotten past their early-season shooting struggles, may have a tough time scoring against the Timberwolves. Even with the recent play of Jalen Brunson, Mikal Bridges, Landry Shamet, and Miles McBride supplementing Karl-Anthony Towns’ dominant season, the Knicks still find themselves outside the top 10 in three-point percentage and near the bottom of the league in field goal percentage. That doesn’t mean the Knicks won’t be able to score, though. They have two very clear advantages heading into tonight.

One advantage is that they’ll have the two best players on the court. The Knicks can say this in a lot of games, and that hasn’t stopped them from getting off to a disappointing 8-6 start. And this matters less in the regular season than it does in the postseason. But this should still bode well for the Knicks. Brunson won Eastern Conference Player of the Week to kick off November and hasn’t really looked back. Even against a tough Raptors defense, he came through and put together back-to-back quality games. And you can make the argument that Towns hasn’t had a single game this season where he hasn’t been great in one way or another. The big man has also had some monstrous games against his former team, averaging 29.0 PPG, 14.3 RPG, and 3.7 APG while shooting 61.7% from the field and 56.3% from three. And in two of those three games, Towns scored 32 or more points and grabbed 13 or more rebounds.

The Knicks’ second advantage comes on the offensive boards. The Timberwolves give up the 12th-most offensive rebounds per game. Some of that is a direct result of their defense forcing so many misses. But with the Knicks being a top-five offensive rebounding team, Towns, as well as Andre Drummond and even Jordan Clarkson, could have big nights on the boards, making up for what could be an inefficient shooting night.

This will be a good test for a Knicks team that has earned seven of its eight wins against teams that are .500 or worse. The Timberwolves are 7-2 at home, deploy a dominant defense predicated on forcing players into the rim-protecting monster that is Gobert, and have a balanced offense that often scores just enough points. But expect the Knicks to lean on their two big horses. Brunson has also had some nice games against the Timberwolves and LaMelo Ball-led teams. And Towns has dominated just about everybody this season. We also can’t forget that the Knicks themselves have a good defense, which could test a limited Timberwolves offense. The Knicks come away with a low-scoring, ugly win led by Towns to improve to 9-6.

Who: New York Knicks (8-6) at Minnesota Timberwolves (11-4)Date: Thursday, November 19, 2026Place: Target Center, Minneapolis, MNFollow: @ptknicksblog and bsky

items.title: 'Passion has no age. Class is timeless' – Solution Tech-Nippo-Rali confirm Domenico Pozzovivo will continue racing at the age of 44
items.author: cyclingnews@futurenet.com (Dani Ostanek)
items.content:
Solution Tech-Nippo-Rali have confirmed that Domenico Pozzovivo will race on with the team next year, the Italian climber continuing in the peloton past his 44th birthday.

"Some riders are part of a team. Others are part of cycling history. Domenico Pozzovivo will continue racing in Solution Tech-Nippo-Rali colours in 2027! Passion has no age. Class is timeless," the team announced on Wednesday.

Pozzovivo, who turns 44 on November 30, has been racing since 2005, with next year marking his 22nd season as a pro. He retired at the end of 2024 as he and his wife Valentina welcomed their first child, Diana, before returning in April on a one-year deal.

Pozzovivo didn't race the Giro d'Italia in 2026 after his team didn't receive an invite, but he told that he's hoping to make a record-breaking 19th appearance at his home Grand Tour next May.

"Now I'm at 18, tied with Wladimiro Panizza, and... yes, I'd like to," he said. "Also because nowadays it's rare for a professional career to last beyond 12-14 years. So it would be a record that, while not unbeatable, could last a long time.

"Competition is the foundation of sport, and yes, I confess that it makes me happy. Finishing ahead of someone less than half my age doubles the satisfaction."

Solution Tech-Nippo-Rali look good for a Giro wildcard invitation next season alongside Polti-VisitiMalta, with Italy's other ProTeam, Bardiani CSF-7 Saber, not eligible for an invitation after missing the top 30 in the UCI rankings.

Pozzovivo would be a leader for the team if they are invited. He finished the season with the second-most UCI points of any rider on the roster, only behind Serbian sprinter Dušan Rajović, and this year achieved a series of eye-catching results at the age of 43.

Highlights of his 2026 season included third-place finishes at the Giro dell'Appennino, GP Beiras a Serra da Estrela, the Czech Tour, and a fourth place at the Mercan'Tour Classic Alpes-Maritimes.

"Between training and races, a million kilometres – actually, even more. At least 1.1 million. And I still haven’t stopped," he told .

"Training isn't a big deal for me, and I enjoy cycling. My performance, considering my age, is decent. So I turn the tables: why shouldn't I? Besides, I'm naturally drawn to challenging myself and my limits. That's the main thing."

Pozzovivo said that he had to negotiate with his wife to continue racing. He's balanced family life with time on the bike, while he has also completed his third degree (studies in nutrition sciences have followed previous degrees in business economics and sports science), with a fourth possibly upcoming.

"It was a fairly long 'negotiation', so to speak. When I stopped, at the end of 2024, one of the reasons was to be as close as possible to my daughter, who was about to be born," he said.

"But I started again because I realised that things could be reconciled, given that cycling is still important but no longer comes first. I'm trying to put it all together, and I think I can do it.

"If you love studying, and I do, it's right to continue doing so because staying up-to-date is essential – keeping up with the latest discoveries in practice. Specifically, I've delved deeper into nutrition sciences because it's something that, in endurance sports, now affects performance by 50%.

"Next year I'd like to take the state exam to become a nutritional biologist. To answer your question... Maybe, but I don't rule out the possibility that I might be interested in a Master's degree."

Now, however, Pozzovivo will turn his focus to training for 2027 and that possible return to the Giro d'Italia, where he's finished in the top 10 on seven occasions. Will it be his final season on the bike?

"We'll see. It's not a given," he concluded.

items.lbText:
New head coach’s first game is at Anfield on Sunday

‘We are going there with the idea to win and be brave’

Mauricio Pochettino has called on Manchester United to have “no fear” when they travel to Anfield on Sunday for his first game. The Argentinian does not want his players to take a backward step as he targets a fast start.

United are 18th in the Premier League and Liverpool fourth but the head coach will not accept any self-doubt. Pochettino is known for being attack-minded and is keen to instil those ideals, but will have had only three days with the players since replacing Michael Carrick.

“We are going to Anfield with the idea to win and be brave and to be Manchester United ,” Pochettino told the club’s website. “The history talks for us, and what we need to expect. We need to be sure that we are brave and we are protagonists and go there with no fears and challenge a very good team like Liverpool.”

Pochettino arrived in Manchester on Wednesday after an overnight flight, having taken charge of his final USA match against Haiti . He toured the training ground and held meetings with senior staff and players not on international duty.

Members of Pochettino’s staff were in place earlier in the week as they seek to revitalise a team with one league win. Pochettino is waiting for United to ratify the appointment of Sílvia Tuyà, a strength and conditioning coach who worked with him with the USA. She travelled with him by private jet to Manchester but was not named among the staff later in the day.

“We need to go little by little, step by step,” Pochettino said. “We cannot go too fast but also we need to, at the same time, attack the priorities to build something.”

He said it was important he and his staff adapt to the culture of the club. “And then, with this sense of knowing the history of the club, try to create all together, because we are all different, a culture, a philosophy that can respect that identity, the history of the club. But at the same time, performing. If we don’t perform, the responsibility is mine.”

Pochettino has coveted the United job and is a keen admirer of Sir Alex Ferguson, whom he describes as “the best coach in history”. Since the Scot’s retirement in 2013, United have failed to match his success but Pochettino said he was looking at “the potential of the club”. The weight of past achievements has hindered individuals over the past 13 years.

“The players need to express their talent,” Pochettino said. “We need to create the environment and the platform for the players to perform. That is the most important thing and that is our priority now: it’s to work with them and try to take the pressure.

“Pressure needs to bring energy, responsibility needs to bring energy. Because if not, it’s too heavy to put all that pressure and responsibility on your back. When you connect with the game, you connect through your talent when you feel freedom, when you feel happy, when you want to play for your teammates, when you want to play for your family, when you want to play for your club, your fans.”

He sounded an upbeat note, saying: “With the power of this club and the fans supporting us, I think we will get in the place that we deserve to be.”

United’s total borrowings have risen to £784.5m, with long-term debt up by almost £100m over the past year. Figures published for the three months to 30 September show long-term borrowings of £577.4m, compared with £481.2m 12 months earlier. United’s cash reserves fell from £80.5m to £55.5m during the same period despite an increase in revenue.

The club reported a quarterly net loss of £18.1m, compared with £6.6m ​in ​the same period a year earlier. Revenue rose by 4% to £146m.

items.title: Tour de Romandie saved as Primeo Energie steps in as sponsor for both women’s and men’s races
items.author: Owen Rogers
items.content:
After a lack of funds was cited as a major contributing factor in the cancellation of the 2026 Tour de Romandie Féminin, the race will return in 2027 with Primeo Energie stepping up to sponsor both women’s and men’s races.

The Swiss electricity company have sponsored the races’ mountains classification jerseys since 2022, the first year of the women’s race, but will now be the main sponsor of both events for the next two editions.

Even before the 2026 race, the organisation was in trouble, hoping to address a 10% budget shortfall by attracting Tadej Pogačar (UAE Team Emirates). But a week after he won four of the five stages and the general classification, organisers, Chassot Concept SA, announced the postponement of the 2026 women’s race.

"This postponement also aims to preserve the Foundation's financial stability and, ultimately, to guarantee the quality and long-term viability of the event," organisers said at the time.

Now, with Primeo Energie on board, not only is the men’s race secure, but the women’s event will return in 2027, with the three-day stage race due to start on September 10th.

"We have seen just how deeply the Tour de Romandie is rooted in the hearts of the people of French-speaking Switzerland," Primeo Energie’s CEO, Cédric Christmann, said. "We are strengthening our presence in a region where we intend to continue our growth.

"Supporting the women’s race is also particularly important to me; women’s cycling deserves more attention - much like the energy sector, especially regarding technical roles and leadership positions."

Unlike the men’s race, which began in 1947, the women’s race has a short history, starting as recently as 2022. Then Ashleigh Moolman-Pasio beat Annemiek van Vleuten on the mountain stage to the ski centre at Thyon 2000, going on to take the only WorldTour general classification success of her career.

Held in 2025, the most recent edition was won by home rider Elise Chabby (FDJ-SUEZ). The race also witnessed the emergence of Paula Blasi, who won the opening day mountain time trial, collecting her first WorldTour victory. However, the race was undermined when five teams were excluded from the race before the start.

While details of the women’s race are yet to be released, organisers chose the sponsorship announcement to publish details of the 80th edition of the men’s race, which will start with its traditional prologue on Tuesday, April 27 and feature a number of circuit-based stages.

"We have opted for loop-style stages, with each one taking place almost entirely within a single canton," said organiser Richard Chassot.

"This allows the public to see the riders multiple times in a festive atmosphere. This format also addresses safety requirements, which are becoming increasingly complex and costly."

  • Prologue - Yverdon-les-Bains (4.7km)
  • Stage 1 - Romont - Romont (170.1km)
  • Stage 2 - La Chaux-de-Fonds - La Chauxde-Fonds (176.2km)
  • Stage 3 - Vully-les-Lacs - Vully-les-Lacs, ITT (14.6km)
  • Stage 4 - Sierre - Sierre (141.7km)
  • Stage 5 - Moutier - Canton du Jura (Distance not yet known)

items.title: Tour Colombia returns for 2027 after two-year break with multiple WorldTour teams expected to race
items.author: cyclingnews@futurenet.com (Dani Ostanek)
items.content:
The early-season Tour Colombia returns to the calendar in 2027, with the race's fifth edition set to run January 26-31.

The race was founded in 2018 as the Colombia Oro y Paz and has run editions in 2019, 2020, and 2024. It was cancelled in both 2025 and 2026 due to financial difficulties.

It's back next season, however, with its return announced in September. Last week, the race was unveiled in a presentation in Medellín attended by former winners Egan Bernal and Sergio Higuita, as well as a host of other Colombian cycling stars, including Santiago Buitrago, Fernando Gaviria, Nairo Quintana, and Rigoberto Urán.

This week, the route for the 2.1-ranked race was unveiled, and the first teams confirmed to take part were also announced.

Colombian outlet has revealed that WorldTour teams Netcompany Ineos and EF Education-EasyPost will be taking part. It's likely, then, that Bernal, Harold Tejada, Iván Sosa, and Juan Felipe Rodríguez will be racing.

US squad Modern Adventure Pro Cycling will also be on the start line, as will Colombian Continental squads NU Colombia (the team of 2024 champion Rodrigo Contreras), Medellín-EPM (featuring Óscar Sevilla), GW Sportfitness, Sistecrédito, and Orgullo Paisa.

reports that NSN, Movistar, and Caja Rural-Seguros RGA could also be at the start.

The most recent edition in 2024 saw Contreras take overall victory by six seconds from Richard Carapaz, then racing for EF, as Mark Cavendish, Nairo Quintana, and Alexey Lutsenko also took part.

Those who are racing will face a six-day run from Medellín to the final summit finish atop the Alto de Palmas. The 904.2km route will be confined to the Antioquia region, with the toughest stages coming in the last two days of the race, including a penultimate stage finish atop the climb to the Alto la Unión.

items.title: Who has the best F1 power unit: Red Bull or Mercedes? Russell shares interesting theory
What the TotalEnergies Exit Means for Netcompany-Ineos
items.author: ahood
items.content: French company TotalEnergies is leaving its deal with Netcompany-Ineos to pivot into the women's peloton and back Demi Vollering.
items.lbText:
TotalEnergies is leaving Netcompany-Ineos in a pivot to women's racing. (Photo: ASPER JACOBS / BELGA MAG / Belga / AFP via Getty Images)

Netcompany-Ineos will lose TotalEnergies as a backer in 2027 just as the former Tour de France powerhouse tries to rebuild its challenge for the yellow jersey.

The departure — first reported by The Athletic and subsequently confirmed by the team — ends a partnership that began ahead of the 2025 Tour. The French energy giant reportedly contributed more than €10 million annually.

That leaves a major hole to fill, but the team did not say reveal the exit will affect its budget.

“We’re grateful to everyone at TotalEnergies for their support and commitment since joining us ahead of the 2025 Tour de France. They’ve been valued partners, and we’re proud to have represented the TotalEnergies brand across two seasons of racing,” a Netcompany-Ineos spokesperson said in a statement to the media.

It’s a financial hit as the team is undergoing a rebuilding effort to regain its spot in the Tour de France conversation.

Danish technology company Netcompany joined as title sponsor in May, reportedly worth around €20 million per season. Ineos remains the team owner and has been searching for new financial partners to help ease the financial cost of the WorldTour team.

Team officials did not reveal how this will impact the team’s budget for 2027.

The team saw high turnover during this year’s transfer season, with Filippo Ganna, Ben Turner, Andrew August, Magnus Sheffield, and Artem Shimdt among several riders leaving.

Though there were no marquee signings, it picked up highly touted junior world champion Benjamín Noval and Riley Sheehan among nine new arrivals for 2027.

At its peak, during the Sky/Ineos era, it won seven Tours with eight different riders from 2012 to 2019, but has not reached the Paris podium since Geraint Thomas finished third in 2022.

Expected race leader Oscar Onley missed this year’s race due to a shoulder injury, and Egan Bernal’s 20th was the team’s top GC.

TotalEnergies, meanwhile, is pivoting its cycling resources into women’s racing .

It exited Jean-René Bernaudeau’s men’s ProTeam squad, which lated landed replacement sponsor XEFI for three seasons through 2029.

This week, the French company also committed to five seasons as co-title title sponsor of Demi Vollering’s team from 2027.

The squad will race as Team TotalEnergies-FDJ United through 2031.

items.title: Giro d’Italia Taps MAAP to Make the Pink Jersey in 2027
items.author: ahood
items.content: MAAP will design the Giro's 'maglia rosa' in 2027 as Castelli replaces Santini at the Tour de France and Vuelta in grand tour leader's jersey reshuffle.
items.lbText:
MAAP is linking up with the Giro d'Italia in bold new deal. (Photo: Gruber Images/MAAP)

MAAP will make and design the Giro d’Italia’s pink jersey in 2027 in a big move for the Melbourne company that built its name on minimalist graphics and high-end performance.

The multi-year agreement with RCS Sport includes the classification jerseys at the Giro d’Italia , Giro d’Italia Women and Giro Next Gen, including the iconic maglia rosa .

“MAAP was founded in Melbourne just 12 years ago. In 2027, we’ll design the ‘maglia rosa,'” cofounder Jarrad Smith said in the announcement. “It’s the race that got me into road cycling.”

MAAP will also supply technical apparel for all RCS races, in both men’s and women’s editions at Strade Bianche, Milano-Sanremo, Il Lombardia, Tirreno-Adriatico, Giro-E, Milano-Torino, Il Giro d’Abruzzo, and GranPiemonte.

Financial terms were not disclosed Thursday when officials confirmed the deal.

MAAP built a following among younger cyclists with its trademark graphics and street-wear cred coupled with top-end performance quality.

The company quickly grew organically and was built by word of mouth into what’s now a global brand.

For RCS, the pivot comes as the Italian grand tour is trying to get younger fans to start adding the Giro into their social media feeds.

“We are confident that the new jerseys, which will be unveiled soon, will generate great interest among all cycling fans, and particularly among younger generations,” said Paolo Bellino, CEO and general manager of RCS Sports and Events.

No one knows. Thursday’s announcement only confirmed the deal.

“The partnership seeks to bridge the deep traditions of European racing with contemporary culture through performance and design,” a statement read.

Based on the PR, it also sounds like there will be special-edition apparel and accessories for each race via “race capsules.”

The first jerseys will be revealed ahead of Milano-Sanremo in March.

The Giro’s switch is part of a leader’s jersey reshuffle across all three grand tours.

Castelli , which supplied the Giro’s pink jersey through this year, will replace Santini at both the Tour de France and the Vuelta a España in 2027.

The Tour is reviving the Castelli partnership that dates back to the days of Greg LeMond and Miguel Indurain in a deal that ran from 1989 to 1994.

The Giro and MAAP link up after the brand worked with the GreenEdge organization and Jayco-AlUla starting in 2025.

Its Pro Aero race suit has been part of stage wins at all three men’s grand tours, the Tour de France Femmes, and a string of WorldTour classics.

Now it will hit the podium every day across the RCS Sport race portfolio.

items.title: 'A bold new visual era' for the maglia rosa as MAAP strikes deal to produce Giro d'Italia leaders' jerseys
items.author: Owen Rogers
items.content:
Australian cycling kit company MAAP is promising an eye-catching revamp of the Giro d’Italia leaders’ jerseys after agreeing a multi-year partnership with organisers RCS to provide apparel across their range of races.

As well as the men’s and women's Giro d'Italia, the agreement will also see the brand providing jerseys for RCS’s other Italian stage races, including Tirreno Adriatico and the Giro Next Gen.

There will also be jerseys for one-day events like Milan-San Remo, Strade Bianche, and Il Lombardia, though they won’t be worn in the race or awarded to winners.

MAAP, which was only founded in 2014, first entered the European pro peloton in 2024, producing a striking design for women’s Continental team Lifeplus-Wahoo, before going further with the current purple Jayco-AlUla and Liv-AlUla Jayco team kits.

To continue in that eye-catching vein, MAAP is promising "a bold new visual era for the most beautiful Grand Tours".

understands the new pink jersey design for men’s and women’s Giro d'Italia will be a significant departure from the old produced by Castelli, though it will not be revealed until sometime in the New Year.

"The partnership seeks to bridge the deep traditions of European racing with contemporary culture through performance and design," MAAP’s press release states.

"Bringing a progressive perspective to some of cycling's most iconic symbols, MAAP will honour the heritage of these events while challenging conventions through a new approach to technical apparel and visual expression."

It’s been a remarkable rise for MAAP, which was founded in 2014 in the Australian city of Melbourne and has always produced kit that looks a little different to that of other companies. Their first team partnership was for Australian Continental team State of the Matter, before partnering with Trinity Racing in 2019.

"From the start, we set out to make the world’s best cycling apparel, paired with a design language that lights up the sport," said company founder Jarrad Smith.

"The Giro d’Italia has shaped the performance and aesthetic of cycling for more than a century, and it holds a special place in my heart. It’s the race that got me into road cycling. Stepping into that living history, and helping progress the Maglia Rosa and some of cycling’s most storied races, is a defining milestone and a privilege. It’s also a statement of our respect for the sport’s history and our passion for where it can go."

CEO and General Manager of RCS Sports and Events Paolo Bellino said: "MAAP is a young and ambitious company, it stands out for its use of technologically advanced materials and its strong design identity. We are confident that the new jerseys, which will be unveiled soon, will generate great interest among all cycling fans, and particularly among younger generations.

"We hope that this partnership with MAAP will lead us into a new era, one that is even more modern and innovative, while continuing to respect the great tradition of the Giro d’Italia and our races."

The deal comes hot on the heels of Castelli’s partnership and sponsorship agreement with ASO to provide leaders’ jerseys for the Tour de France, Tour de France Femmes and their other races, including both men’s and women’s Vuelta a España, though it is thought the sponsorship element of MAAP’s deal is absent.

How Premier League's big six keep getting richer
items.content: <article>Ten games into the Premier League season, and the top five places are dominated by big six clubs. It should come as no surprise as they have a growing advantage of hundreds of millions of pounds.</article>
items.lbText:
Ten games into the Premier League season, four of the top six spots are occupied by 'big six' clubs.

Only second-placed Brighton , a club with a model which must be the envy of many of their rivals, and Premier League ever-presents Everton , have muscled their way in.

In pure financial terms, it should come as no surprise.

The six biggest clubs - Manchester United , Liverpool , Manchester City , Arsenal , Tottenham and Chelsea - now generate hundreds of millions of pounds more than the division's other teams.

BBC Sport breaks down how the finances of the big six have exploded, examines new trends and the impact on the transfer market, and asks how much it really matters.

Companies put their money where supporters are prepared to spend it. It is a simple fact of business in every country, a reality of football's food chain.

In England, Liverpool , Arsenal and Manchester United traditionally dominated viewing figures, column inches, shirt sales and sponsorship.

Over the past 20 years they have been joined by Chelsea , Manchester City and Tottenham .

This group of clubs now generate so much money it is hard to imagine how they can fail in the long term - even factoring in short-term performance issues.

We will use Everton , the only club not in the big six to be in the Premier League since its inception in 1992.

This tells a tale of how even one of the league's founding members can be left trailing well behind.

In 2009-10, the gap in revenues between the big-six average and Everton was £120m. In 2024-25, that gap had grown to £442m.

So what has driven this huge escalation?

In large part it is the boom in international TV rights.

Kieran Maguire, professor of football finance at the University of Liverpool , told BBC Sport that it has attracted companies prepared to pay large sums to be associated with the Premier League's top clubs.

"The big football brand clubs have global fanbases and that makes them very attractive to global commercial partners, especially for sponsorship and front-of-shirt deals," Maguire said.

"You combine that with the fact that the Premier League is broadcast to 190 different countries around the world, and especially the international audiences - that allows the clubs to negotiate very good prices."

Only 10% of Everton 's revenue comes from commercial deals, while for the big six it is 45%.

It means Everton , and other clubs in the league, are heavily reliant on broadcast income. It makes up 66% of their revenue.

For Everton at least, this should change following the move to Hill Dickinson Stadium.

But that is unlikely to be enough to stop the gap increasing.

It has taken a few years, but Aston Villa and Newcastle have begun to increase their revenue.

This is largely thanks to the financial rewards of Champions League football.

But even Uefa has created a system which entrenches the position of the biggest clubs.

When the European Super League plan was torpedoed, Uefa created a new financial deal called the value pillar.

This reserves 35% of all Champions League revenues, or £713m, for the historically most successful clubs.

At the end of the league phase last season City are estimated to have earned £37.9m from the value pillar, Liverpool £35.5m and Chelsea £33.3m. Newcastle received only £13.6m.

The good news for Villa is their coefficient has improved greatly, aided by last season's Europa League win.

Their value pillar is projected to be worth £25m this season. But that will still be less than the big six clubs in the competition.

The cards are stacked against an ambitious club - not just domestically, but in Europe too.

Take a look at the financial trend of the big six and one thing becomes noticeable - Chelsea are beginning to fall behind.

In the past two seasons, and for the first time in recent history, the Blues recorded the lowest revenues of the big six.

Not just by a small amount. They were £74m behind Tottenham , and £200m below Liverpool and City.

Stamford Bridge has a capacity of only 40,000, with no easy scope for expansion. The rest of the big six have grounds which hold at least 60,000.

Chelsea generated an average spend per fan of £80 in 2024-25, the second highest in the league after Arsenal .

Yet with 20,000 fewer tickets sold than their big six rivals, Chelsea 's total matchday revenues are dwarfed.

"Matchday spend has become increasingly important," Maguire said. "There has been a flatlining of broadcast revenues, especially since 2017.

"As a consequence, clubs have had to look at alternative methods of increasing revenues, especially with costs both on the pitch and off pitch rising so fast."

Matchday revenue has effectively stalled for Chelsea , rising only £16m over the past 10 years. United's has grown by £69m and Spurs , thanks to their new ground, by £85m.

" Chelsea are far more reliant upon player sales," Maguire said. "There is a growing divide because the global appeal is very much aligned with three or four clubs.

" Arsenal have re-established themselves with their progress in the Champions League. Manchester United are a brand in their own right. And Liverpool have expanded Anfield from 44,000 to 61,000, with many of those extra seats having gone to commercial."

Chelsea 's successful player trading model has so far limited the impact.

But there are signs that, financially at least, the big six could become the big five.

You might recall that Villa and Newcastle were not fans of the old profit and sustainability rules (PSR).

PSR forced both clubs to sell some of their best players to balance the books.

That has changed this season with squad-cost ratio (SCR).

There is a key difference with SCR, in that it allows a club to spend the money they generate on players. PSR limited losses so was more restrictive.

"This does make it a little easier for the likes of Villa and Newcastle to spend money," Maguire said. "But it is still heavily weighted in favour of the big six.…

items.title: Verstappen 'trusts' F1 over Middle East decision
items.content: <article>Max Verstappen says he trusts in Formula 1 after their decision to end the season in the Middle East, despite the ongoing conflicts in the area. </article>
items.lbText:
Max Verstappen says he "trusts" Formula 1 has made the right decision in pressing ahead with the final two races of the season in the Middle East.

Last week, F1 stood down preparations for a substitute race at Imola in Italy if the events in Qatar and Abu Dhabi could not be held because of ongoing conflicts in the area.

The sport will now conclude the season in the Middle East, unless the situation deteriorates before the Qatar event on 27-29 November and Abu Dhabi on 4-6 December.

Verstappen said: "I trust F1 and FIA to make the right call on that, right?

"I don't have all the intel. I'm not an officer. I just hope that they make the right call on that. And that's all that you can rely on, really.

"They also send over their findings and understanding. So I trust them."

No trust problem with Ferrari team - Hamilton

How sporting events are being affected by Middle East conflict

Yamaha will not travel to Qatar for MotoGP race

Verstappen had previously voiced his opposition to ending the season in the Middle East.

"Normally I am happy to go to Qatar and Abu Dhabi, but you know, when there is a war nearby, and if some of the countries are in conflict with each other, then I think we shouldn't go," Verstappen said in September.

The Red Bull driver's fresh remarks reflect a uniform public stance in F1 on the situation, even though there are widespread misgivings among personnel about travelling to the Middle East in the context of the two conflicts in the area.

Last Sunday Iran targeted a US military base in Bahrain with a drone attack for the second time in three days, the latest salvo in the war launched against the country by the US and Israel in February.

And Houthi rebels in Yemen are advancing in their war against the Saudi-backed government of the country.

Missile attacks from the Houthis into Saudi Arabia are threatening that country's chances of hosting the second grand prix of next season, which is scheduled for 19-21 March.

McLaren's Lando Norris said that while he is "fine" with the decision to race, he is concerned about the "big team" behind him.

"I have my friend's wedding in Bahrain next week, so I was planning on going there and then going on to Qatar and then Abu Dhabi," he added.

"But it's not about me. It's a lot more people. It's the fans, it's the team personnel, so the question is for them, more than I would say it is for myself."

Mercedes driver George Russell said he has "no hesitation" in racing and that while he's "sure some people have their reservations" he doesn't "know of anyone who's concerned".

"I know people who live in the region and they said it quite bluntly, if they didn't feel comfortable they wouldn't be there with their families," he said.

"When you look around the world there are a lot of terrible things going on.

"You've just got to trust in the people. If they say it's safe, then you trust in them. F1 aren't stupid and I'm sure there's plans A, B, C, D, etc. So fingers crossed it'll all be fine."

MotoGP, which is owned by the same US group as F1, held a race in Qatar last weekend without problems.

F1, which has significant commercial links with the Middle East, has been closely monitoring the situation and has been advised by security officials and government figures in the Gulf and Europe that the races can go ahead, and there is no official advice against travelling to Qatar or Abu Dhabi.

F1 said in a statement last week that it was still prepared to cancel the two races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi if the situation deteriorated.

"If the situation develops negatively in the coming weeks before the events in the Middle East, we will not hesitate to do the right thing and the safety of everyone will always be the priority," an F1 spokesperson said on Tuesday.

items.title: No trust problem with Ferrari team - Hamilton
items.content: <article>Lewis Hamilton says Ferrari are "super united" despite two recent incidents in which the British driver ignored a team call to pit for fresh tyres.</article>
items.lbText:
Lewis Hamilton says there is "definitely not" a trust problem between him and his Ferrari team.

The seven-time champion has twice in the past four races ignored a call to pit for fresh tyres, both times to his competitive disadvantage.

The most recent time, in the Sao Paulo Grand Prix on 8 November, Hamilton stayed out on worn slick tyres in worsening rain and ended up spinning before pitting on the next lap.

Before this weekend's Las Vegas Grand Prix, Hamilton spoke positively of his relationship with his race engineer Carlo Santi.

"We're constantly working on our communication," said Hamilton, who had a different race engineer last year.

"It's been a lot better this year. Carlos (sic) has done an amazing job. And those particular two times, particularly the last time, was just I didn't have the information I needed. I got the call right at the last minute.

"We'll just continue to work on the processes. We're super united in what's working, in the right direction."

The previous time Hamilton ignored a call to pit was in Singapore, when he decided to stay out during a virtual safety car period. He later apologised .

At the following race in Austin, he explained that he was "always looking at ways to win, always looking at doing potentially something different. And I wanted to be on a different strategy, not just the same strategy as Charles (Leclerc), where we just follow each other".

Ferrari's Hamilton-Leclerc problem - and other F1 stories to follow

'We've got big problems' - Hamilton says Ferrari need 'serious talks'

Verstappen 'trusts' F1 over Middle East decision

Hamilton and Leclerc both insisted that relations between the pair were good after clear-the-air talks in Brazil following a disagreement at the previous race in Mexico, where a tangle on the first lap led to them throwing away a potential one-two and handing victory to Red Bull's Max Verstappen.

Hamilton said in Las Vegas on Wednesday: "Charles is a great driver. The detail we went into about stuff like that in terms of when we close the visor, it's very clear we understand each other.

"We understand each other's boundaries and the ultimate goal, which is to get the best result for the team.

"So I don't feel that that will be a problem going forward. I have no concerns or worries about racing him, and I don't think he does with me either."

Leclerc said: "The discussion went very well. Very, very quickly, after a few sentences already, the tension that was there was not there anymore, and it was all fine.

"We both work in the direction of having that second place in the constructors' championship. The second place in the constructors' is important.

"It's also true that we've got a relatively big margin behind, which doesn't mean we need to minimise that, and we still have to work as a team. But what is really important for me now is to try and win before the end of the season and win the race."

He added that "everything has been taken out of proportion" but he is "kind of used to it" have been at Ferrari since 2019.

"Of course, the goal is not always to agree, and that will never happen," he added.

"We can have different opinions, and that was the case, for example, in Mexico. But just the fact of speaking eased all tensions, and we were completely fine with it.

"It's not that we had to speak for an hour, even though it ended up lasting an hour, just because we had a good time and we started speaking about also many other things in trying to bring the team and to help the team go forward.

"But the discussion about the tension was like maybe five or 10 minutes, and then the air was clean, and that's it."

The Avinox Motor Disrupted e-MTB. Now It’s Coming for Your Commute.
items.author: Josh Ross
items.content: Amflow expands beyond the trail with the carbon UE Series, pairing 125 Nm of torque with electronic shifting and integrated tech for city riding.
items.lbText:
This week, Amflow is expanding beyond electric mountain bikes with the launch of its first city commuter line, the Amflow UE Series. On the surface, it sounds like yet another unfamiliar name offering a high-powered commuter bike, but the news is a bit bigger than that. What this really means is that DJI-backed Amflow and its Avinox motor are making the jump from e-MTB to city riding.

Available now in the UE Carbon and UE Carbon Pro builds, the platform pairs that drive system with a claimed 2.35-kilogram full-carbon, low step-through frame to hit a complete bike weight of 20.9 kilograms, or roughly 46 pounds. It makes for an impressive offering on paper and raises the obvious question of whether putting that kind of hardware into a transportation-focused package will reshape the commuter market the same way Amflow did e-MTB.

Rather than offering a traditional multi-size run at launch, Amflow designed the standard UE frame to accommodate riders between 5 feet, 1 inch and 6 feet, 3 inches using two interchangeable stem heights. A dedicated small frame for riders between 4 feet, 7 inches and 5 feet, 3 inches is scheduled to arrive in 2027.

Beyond that, the bike follows expected commuter design patterns, leaning toward comfort and visibility. The first lever of that focus is frame geometry, starting with a step-through frame and flat handlebars to put the rider in an upright position. That layout is paired with 65 mm of front suspension, a seatpost with 125 mm of height adjustment and 30 mm of suspension travel, and wide 26×2.0-inch Maxxis tires. Braking comes from Magura 180 mm disc brakes with three-finger levers. For hauling cargo, Amflow equips the bike with a front rack rated for 20 kilograms (about 44 pounds) and a rear MIK HD-compatible rack rated for 27 kilograms (about 59.5 pounds).

The biggest news here is that the motor that disrupted the e-MTB market is expanding into new territory. Powering both builds is the Avinox M2 drive unit, which Amflow claims delivers up to 125 Nm of torque and an 8-to-1 maximum assist ratio. According to the brand, the motor can climb 30% grades under load while keeping operating noise below 45 dBA. The system also includes a traction control feature and a new Auto Boost mode that automatically increases power output on steep hills or loaded starts without rider input.

Both builds use a removable 600Wh battery, with Amflow claiming a maximum range of 132 kilometers (about 82 miles) under controlled testing conditions. It charges from zero to 100% in 2 hours and 23 minutes, and riders can set a custom charge limit to preserve cell longevity.

Both models also feature electronic shifting with automatic and smooth-shifting modes, leaving the drivetrain as the main mechanical difference between the two. The UE Carbon Pro uses a custom three-speed electronic internal geared hub paired with a Gates carbon belt, which allows riders to shift while stopped and avoids chain maintenance or greasy clothes — though it costs more. Alternatively, the less expensive Amflow UE Carbon uses a 10-speed electronic rear derailleur co-developed with TRP.

Amflow leans heavily into its connected ecosystem on the UE Series, integrating several new Avinox accessories directly into the bike. Control centers on a 1.4-inch DP200 handlebar touchscreen paired with a rotating phone mount that offers 15W wireless and 20W USB-C charging. The integrated lighting system features automatic dusk activation, high- and low-beam switching and a brake-sensing rear light.

Through the Avinox Ride app, riders can pair multiple bikes to one account, merge ride files, sync with an Apple Watch and control compatible DJI Osmo cameras from the handlebar. The system can also pair with a heart rate monitor to adjust motor assist automatically based on a target heart rate zone.

On the security front, a single key operates both the battery lock and an integrated 10 mm hardened steel ART 2-Star horseshoe lock. The bike also supports Apple Find My tracking and an app-based Lost Mode designed to disable the bike remotely if it is stolen.

Both the Amflow UE Carbon and UE Carbon Pro are available immediately through Amflow’s website and authorized dealers. U.S. pricing is $3,499 for the UE Carbon and $3,899 for the UE Carbon Pro.

items.title: Manchester United’s infamous 1974 relegation is a warning from history
items.author: Sam Cunningham
items.content:
It may have been a different era, but the 1970s contain salutary lessons for a club in serious decline once again

In many ways, there are striking parallels between the Manchester United relegated in 1974 and the Manchester United sitting in the relegation zone at this stage of the season for the first time in 40 years. A legendary manager leaves, his shadow remains; with boardroom dithering and uncertainty, his replacements churn and burn as the club slide over several years.

Sir Matt Busby stepped aside as manager of the 1968 European Cup-winning side, but stayed on as a director, just as Sir Alex Ferguson did, watching from the Old Trafford directors’ box as successors tried and failed.

items.lbText:
It may have been a different era, but the 1970s contain salutary lessons for a club in serious decline once again

I n many ways, there are striking parallels between the Manchester United relegated in 1974 and the Manchester United sitting in the relegation zone at this stage of the season for the first time in 40 years. A legendary manager leaves, his shadow remains; with boardroom dithering and uncertainty, his replacements churn and burn as the club slide over several years.

Sir Matt Busby stepped aside as manager of the 1968 European Cup-winning side, but stayed on as a director, just as Sir Alex Ferguson did, watching from the Old Trafford directors’ box as successors tried and failed.

In the six years after being crowned kings of Europe, United turned to Wilf McGuinness, Busby stepped in temporarily to keep them up, then Frank O’Farrell was appointed before they landed on Tommy Docherty, who experienced the ignominy of taking them down.

In the past eight years, United have sacked José Mourinho, Ole Gunnar Solskjær, Erik ten Hag , Ruben Amorim and now Michael Carrick .

How did the United of 1974 go down? Most outsiders believed they were too big to fail. Inside the club, though, they sensed the direction of travel. After a heavy defeat at Crystal Palace in December 1972, Busby offered Docherty the job in the Selhurst Park boardroom. “There’s a lot of trouble in the camp,” Busby said. Docherty was doing well as Scotland manager and took a few days to mull it over, but decided he couldn’t turn down the opportunity.

When Busby called him on the Sunday evening, he accepted. “You know it won’t be easy?” Busby said. “It’ll be like turning an oil tanker round, only bigger.” He added: “You might find yourself having to take a step back in order to take a leap forward.” Docherty wrote in his autobiography, The Doc, that at the time he never believed Busby was alluding to relegation.

Docherty was given free rein for a rebuild. The day after his appointment, he signed George Graham from Arsenal for £120,000, a sizeable fee at the time. Alex Forsyth followed from Partick for £100,000 and Docherty pulled off a coup when he persuaded Lou Macari to join bottom-of-the-table United instead of Liverpool for £200,000.

The giants of the previous era were moved on. In February, Bobby Charlton told him that, at 37, it would be his last season. Other big names wanted to stay, but Docherty felt a reset was needed. “The Manchester United team that had won the European Cup in 1968 was without a doubt a great team, but many members of that side had been allowed to grow old together,” he wrote.

“I knew what I had decided would prove very unpopular with many people but it had to be done. I set out my stall to end the United careers of among others Denis Law, Tony Dunne, Pat Crerand and David Sadler.”

George Best, who had retired once but returned under Docherty, played his last game on New Year’s Day 1974 after repeatedly turning up late. The most controversial departure was Law, who was allowed to join Manchester City.

Having taken over with United bottom, Docherty kept them up in his first season and was emboldened to continue his clearout. Thirteen players were released that summer. But halfway through the following season they were facing relegation again and a lack of goals cost them. At one stage, the joint-top scorer was Alex Stepney, with two penalties. He was the goalkeeper.

Relegation was confirmed on the penultimate day as they lost to City, a defeat made all the more painful by Law back-heeling the late winner. Docherty was interviewed on the Old Trafford pitch and asked, in a scene replayed in TNT Sports’ Too Good To Go Down, whether the club would drift into obscurity. “No, there’s no danger,” he said. “We could wash the jerseys here and hang them out to dry and you’d get 15,000 people standing watching them do so.”

Despite the bravado, Docherty was expecting the sack when he met Busby a few days later. Instead, Busby handed him a case of champagne, reminded him of the oil tanker and told him to set to work getting them back up.

Docherty’s prediction proved right: the brand was far bigger than the division they played in. In the Second Division, Old Trafford averaged crowds of more than 47,000 – the biggest in the country – and their away support descended on towns and cities and routinely outnumbered the home contingent.

Docherty bought young and hungry, targeting players with a point to prove, including Steve Coppell from Tranmere, Stuart Pearson from Hull and Jim Holton from Shrewsbury. The direct, attacking football synonymous with United returned and the Scot shaped a fearless 4-2-4 formation.

Crowds grew after they came straight back up and for a while United were on course to become the fifth side to win the First Division after promotion, but finished third and also reached the FA Cup final, losing 1-0 to Southampton. That shows the stark differences between then and now.

The gap between the first and second tiers was narrower. United did not lose a gargantuan broadcast deal when they went down. They were not saddled with debt by their owners. Their wage bill was not tied to Champions League qualification. Players were not on long contracts and were easier to buy and sell. There were no disruptive agents. Fans were more patient.

If lessons of the 1970s are not heeded soon, the fallout could be infinitely more painful.

items.title: The Tech Editor’s Guide to Black Friday Cycling Deals
items.author: Josh Ross
items.content: We skipped the clearance bin leftovers to bring you a heavily vetted list of the only Black Friday cycling sales actually worth your money.
items.lbText:
If you buy through our links, we may earn an affiliate commission. This supports our mission to get more people active and outside. Learn about Outside Online's affiliate link policy

Black Friday in the cycling industry is, more often than not, just an excuse for brands to clear out last year’s weird colors, odd sizes, and sub-par gear that didn’t sell. It’s easy to get lured in by a massive discount and end up with equipment that doesn’t actually perform under pressure.

That’s not what this list is. I spend the entire year testing the best road and gravel gear on the market, and that’s what I’ve gone looking for. I’ve combed through the noise to find the actual discounts on equipment that earns its keep. Whether it’s premium apparel or major tech upgrades, I’m only tracking the Black Friday sales on gear I would genuinely recommend buying at full price

If you are using these sales to knock out your holiday shopping, treat this list as a companion to our buyer’s guides. My recent Road Bike Gifts They Actually Want This Year , along with our guides to the best winter cycling jackets (and the best women’s cycling jackets) , best bike computers , the best bike lights , the best smart trainers , or the best headphones for cycling represent the equipment I consider the absolute best of the best. I’ll do my best to look through all of it and find the things that are on sale, but because sale inventory moves fast, those guides are also worth checking.

You are here reading this list on Velo where our editors work hard to bring interesting and unique perspectives on cycling. We are also part of the greater Outside network and an Outside+ subscription drops any paywall on Velo plus adds unlimited digital access to 10+ publications in the Outside Network, print edition of Outside magazine delivered quarterly, digital access to the Outside Magazine print edition, premium maps in the Gaia GPS app, full trail access in the Trailforks app, advanced insights in MapMyFitness, weather tools from Meteo365, and unlimited streaming on Outside TV. Your purchase gets you added benefits and helps support the content you love.

I actually have this helmet in the best bike helmet’s buyers guide and I love it. It has ebike certification but I also love that it has the right style for the application. I don’t know what else i could possibly replace it with in the guide but for more than 50% off this is a great buy.

Logan Jones-Wilkins added these to his list of gravel cyclist gifts saying “I have dropped them, shoved them in pockets, and sat on them, and they have survived without a single scratch to show for it.” Now even if you do manage to break them, you can get a backup pair.

That image is the Knog Blinder 900 which has since been replaced with a more powerful unit for the same price. Except right now it’s even cheaper and it’s bundled with a rear light. I love the mounting system and at under $100 for a pair of lights that will manage both tons of commuting and serious adventure, this is a steal.

Road cyclists love a good pair of socks. Just the right height and color plus they have to stay up. Silca nails it with their aero socks and the brand also claims watts saved. You won’t won’t go wrong with these as a gift. Oh and there’s white too, I just like the bright pink.

I have a lot of Roka sunglasses and they are all fantastic. You can’t go wrong with classic aviators.

Lisa clearly love the photochromatic option.

I wrote a whole article about the Silca Wax System and why I don’t care about the performance benefits but I love this system anyway. I feel like this is one of those things a lot of people are not sure about buying but have been considering. It’s a great product and you can help give someone the final push.

If you want music while you ride your bike, bone conduction headphones are far and away the best option and Shokz are the most popular. The brand is actually running a bunch of different sales so you might find something you like better but I prefer the OpenRun 2 on the bike. I love that a single button press stops the music and once you’ve done that you can leave them in place with no ill effect. Go for the mini if you don’t need to fit long hair under the band and it’ll stay out of the way better.

One of the best things about Garmin is the way that the ecosystem lets you move between devices seamlessly. I don’t have to wear a strap or a watch while I ride because I have a Garmin bike computer. When I get off the bike and put on the watch, the data seamlessly switches so that it’s all uninterrupted in Garmin Connect. That opens up a small need for something different in my watch, though. I want something that looks good and works as a smartwatch as much as a fitness watch. That’s where the Garmin Venu X1 fits in. Bonus here is that it’s got a massive discount for the holidays.

If you are looking for a smart trainer this winter, just buy this one. The KICKR CORE is the benchmark for smart trainers and while you can get extra features for more money, it has everything you need. It’s a great deal at its regular price but this is as cheap as it ever gets and right now it also comes with a coupon for one free month of Zwift Plus in the box. items.title: Bottas' stay at Cadillac confirmed for 2027
items.content: <article>Valtteri Bottas is retained by Cadillac for the 2027 Formula 1 season.</article>
items.lbText:
Valtteri Bottas has been retained by Cadillac for the 2027 Formula 1 season.

The future of the 37-year-old Finn had been in doubt as the American team endure a difficult maiden campaign.

To date, they have failed to collect a point in either the drivers' or constructors' championship.

However, two-time championship runner-up Bottas will race again with them next year.

"I'm excited to continue this journey with Cadillac into 2027," said Bottas, who is preparing for Sunday's Las Vegas Grand Prix.

"We knew building a new Formula One team from the ground up wasn't going to be easy, but that's exactly what makes this challenge so special.

"We've laid the foundations, we're learning and improving, and there's still plenty more to come. I'm hungry for more, and I believe in what we're building together. The story is only just getting started."

The news follows the recent announcement that Mexican Sergio Perez, 36, will also be remaining with Cadillac until 2029 after signing a contract extension.

Cadillac had been considering whether to promote their American reserve driver, Colton Herta, into Bottas' seat.

The 26-year-old former Indycar driver has earned enough points to apply for the superlicence required to drive in F1 through his outings in practice this year.

But the feeling was that there was no obvious upgrade to Bottas and that the Finn had not been given a fair run in what has been a difficult debut season for Cadillac beset by reliability problems and lack of pace.

The team decided that they needed stability for their second season, and that the experience provided by Perez and Bottas, who have both won grands prix, was as important as ever.

Herta had given up his seat in Indycar to drive in Formula 2 this season with the idea of preparing himself for F1.

However, he has had a difficult season and lies 19th in the championship with two races remaining.

Herta now faces a decision as to what to do in 2027.

Cadillac are still open to the idea of him graduating to F1, perhaps in 2028, but it is not clear where he may race next year while he waits to see whether that opportunity arises.

TWG, the US consortium which runs Cadillac, has other teams in other categories for which Herta could race alongside any F1 reserve role that might be on offer.

One of the options would involve a return to Indycar, or Herta could perhaps move into endurance racing.

Whatever happened to the diamond that went missing in F1 crash?

Cowboy boots, cocktails and casinos - how do three US grands prix compare?

items.title: The longest single-opponent winning streaks in Knicks history
items.author: Michael Zeno
items.content:
On Tuesday night, the Knicks outlasted the Raptors for the second time in three nights to extend a staggering 15-game winning streak against their Canadian rivals that dates back to January 2023.

Beyond the fact that it means that old friends RJ Barrett and Immanuel Quickley have never beaten their old team, it also extends one of the longest streaks in program history against a single opponent.

Celtics, 21 games (1993-98)

As mentioned on last night’s broadcast, it’s hard to believe such a dominant stretch existed against a longtime rival that has been the Eastern Conference’s banner of success for generations.

Simply, the sport is cyclical, and the few times the Celtics were in the doldrums, the Knicks were contending for titles. Through the many dark ages of Knicks history, the Celtics dominated. It’s why they’ve only faced off in the postseason three times in the last 35 years.

From 1965-67, the Celtics won 21 in a row against the Knicks in the heart of the Bill Russell era. It took 25 years to return the favor.

On January 10, 1993, the Celtics outlasted the Knicks at TD Garden in a 100-97 win. They wouldn’t win another game in this rivalry for over five years.

The Celtics won 48 games in 1992-93, but quickly fell into the East’s cellar. They wouldn’t win 40 games again in a season until 2001-02, while at the same time, Patrick Ewing and the Knicks had only the Bulls and Pacers competing with them for spots in the NBA Finals yearly.

Ewing would score 65 combined over the next two meetings in April 1993 before scoring 30 again on Opening Night that October in a three-point win in Boston. He routinely owned the Celtics during this time, reaching a crescendo with a 36-14 effort in March 1994.

As the Celtics got worse, the Knicks took advantage of them more and more. A 35-point blowout in February 1994 still stands as one of the biggest blowouts in the rivalry’s history. Hubert Davis nailed five threes and scored 25 points in a 90-83 win the following month.

It was always a different enemy that flummoxed the Celtics. Charles Smith scoring 25, Anthony Mason scoring 21, and John Starks and Ewing’s consistency. Even as Pat Riley turned into Jeff Van Gundy, the Knicks never lost a step.

The streak had reached 17 by January 28, 1997, when the pitiful 9-30 Celtics put the greatest scare into the contending Knicks yet. An eight-point lead in the final minutes dwindled to a tie on a Todd Day three in the final minute before free throws by Antoine Walker gave Boston the lead in the final minute.

Just when the streak appeared over, Chris Childs called game with eight seconds left.

Eventually, the streak would finally end on January 26, 1998, when the Knicks were held to just 85 points behind a 25-point gem by Chauncey Billups. Even this triumphant victory came with an asterisk, as Ewing missed the game due to wrist surgery. Huh.

Cavaliers, 18 games (1980-83)

The Knicks own the Cavs in the playoffs, but did you know there was a stretch they owned them like

In five all-time playoff meetings, the Knicks are 16-2 against the Cavs, but once took things to another level in the early 1980s.

Unlike the Celtics, this is pretty peculiar. The Knicks were an average team during this streak, but took advantage of one of the worst eras of Cavs basketball under Ted Stepien.

Quite precisely, this streak can be known as the “Stepien Streak”, as while he was owner from April 1980 to his sale in April 1983, the Cavs went 1-16 against the Knicks, with the lone win coming just two weeks before he sold the team in late March of 1983.

Highlights of the streak include Mike Glenn’s 29-point game in November 1980 (second-highest scoring game of his career), Ray Williams’ 37-point gem in an overtime win two weeks later, and perennially playing in front of 4,000 fans at an empty Richfield Coliseum. The NBA was totally different in the 80s.

Bullets, 17 games (1952-53)

Back in the day, there weren’t many teams. As such, you get stuff like this.

Over a span of 400 days from February 6, 1952, to March 11, 1953, the Knicks played the Baltimore Bullets 17 times and won every single one of them.

The 1950s Knicks can sometimes be referred to as the Silver Era of Knicks basketball due to the team making multiple Finals appearances before Russell came and made the East his own, so it’s no surprise they were dominant. But like this?

The lore of 1950s NBA is quite fascinating. These teams played each other three times in six days in February 1952 when the streak began, but played the games in three different places. The Bullets won 82-81 in the Baltimore Coliseum on February 4, the Knicks won 73-70 at the 69th Regiment Armory on February 6, and the two teams met in Philadelphia on February 8 in a 20-point blowout win for Ray Lumpp and the Knicks.

On March 5, the teams participated in a doubleheader at the Boston Garden, preceding a game between the Bucks and Celtics later that night.

In 1952-53, when the Knicks went 10-0 against the Bullets en route to a Finals appearance, they played one game in Philly, two games in Boston (one of which went to triple overtime), and even played in Trenton, New Jersey, on March 5, 1953.

Finally, the Bullets snapped the skid on November 14, 1953, behind 19 points by Max Zaslofsky in Baltimore.

Just for the hell of it, here’s some other weird neutral site locations from the 1950s:

  • January 29, 1952, in Louisville (vs. Indianapolis Olympians)
  • February 3, 1953, in Buffalo (vs. Milwaukee Hawks)
  • February 18, 1953, in Providence (vs. Boston Celtics)
  • January 22, 1954, in New Haven, CT (vs. Philadelphia Warriors)
  • Several times in 1954-55 in Miami (vs. Fort Wayne Pistons)
  • November 18, 1954, in Syracuse (vs. Philadelphia Warriors)
  • March 3, 1955, in Saratoga Springs (vs. Milwaukee Hawks)
  • March 13, 1956, in Moorhead, MN (vs. Minneapolis Lakers)
  • January 17, 1957, in Lacrosse, WI (vs. Minneapolis Lakers)
  • January 14, 1958, in St. Louis (vs. Cincinnati Royals)
  • February 21, 1958, in Camden, NJ (vs. Philadelphia Warriors)
  • January 22, 1962, in Moline, IL (vs. Chicago Packers)
  • March 12, 1962, in Seattle (vs. Los Angeles Lakers)
  • Various times in Hershey, PA (including the Wilt 100 game)

Pistons, 16 games (2020-24)

We’ve seen a new standard of excellence for the Knicks since the turn of the decade, They have three of these streaks in the last six years!

Back when the Pistons weren’t the annoying playoff contenders we know them as now, they were pretty damn awful. For years, it was a running joke that the COVID-19 pandemic was younger than the last Pistons win over the Knicks.

The streak began on February 8, 2020, when the Knicks overcame an early double-digit deficit to outlast the Pistons in Detroit in a battle of two lowly teams that wouldn’t even be invited to the bubble. Another win on March 8 would mark the team’s final home game with fans for another year due to the pandemic.

As the Knicks ascended, the Pistons stayed bad. On April 4, 2021, the Knicks eviscerated them by a 125-81 margin, the second-biggest blowout in the over 430 games in this matchup.

Even as the meltdown in 2021-22 ensued, the orange and blue survived a scare that March when Marvin Bagley III dropped 27, only for Alec Burks to strip Cade Cunningham in the final seconds to hold on.

The most memorable game of the streak came at the end. Facing the 8-48 Pistons at home in late February, the Knicks came out sleepy and watched as Cunningham nearly dragged his hapless team to the finish line to end the skid at 14, but shenanigans ensued with Donte DiVincenzo to somehow pull it off with a Josh Hart and-1.

Was it a foul? Does anyone really care?

The streak ended on December 7, 2024. We didn’t know it at the time, but the Pistons had finally emerged as threats, and they’d start their own six-game regular-season winning streak against the Knicks that lasted until three weeks ago.

Raptors and Nets, 15 games (active)

The last time the Raptors beat the Knicks? January 22, 2023.

The last time the Nets beat the Knicks? January 28, 2023.

The next opportunity for both to beat the Knicks? Brooklyn gets another chance on December 27, while Toronto next gets a crack on January 20. It’ll be basically four years for both since their last win.

These two streaks are tied for the fourth-longest active streaks in the NBA.

The three longer? OKC over Memphis, Cleveland over Washington, and the Clippers over the Hornets, all at 17. If you thought four years was a lot, it’s been almost 10 since the Hornets beat the Clippers!

These two streaks are very different, but also the same. Both teams have been worse than the Knicks this entire time, sometimes considerably worse, and have yielded some ugly blowouts.

There have also been plenty of scares. There’s the Brunson game-winner in the NBA Cup, the KAT heroics in The Six, the times that Brooklyn puts up a fight but folds late at Barclays Center, and the multiple double-digit comebacks we saw this week.

Either way, those are two Atlantic Division rivals that can’t beat the Knicks. It also comes directly after both dominated the Knicks for prolonged periods.

Remember Nic Claxton’s comments? Well, at the time, the Knicks were 0-9 against the Nets from 2020-23.

The Raptors went a blistering 23-5 against the Knicks from January 2016 to November 2023.

Ain’t no fun when the rabbit’s got the gun.

items.title: 24 teams come together to form Collective Cycling Group, the latest venture aiming to 'unlock the value' of pro cycling
items.author: laura.weislo@futurenet.com (Laura Weislo)
items.content:
Following the collapse of the One Cycling project that aimed to reform professional cycling into a more lucrative business model, a new group has officially made its presence known with similar aims but stronger support. The Collective Cycling Group (CCG) issued a press release on Wednesday announcing the new movement.

It was stated that 24 teams from the men’s and women’s WorldTour and ProTeam ranks have already signed up, and that there are ongoing discussions with additional teams. Several teams have shared news of the announcement, indicating that they are part of the movement, but not all have.

The CCG aims to "develop and market selected commercial rights and activities to strengthen the economic model of professional cycling", according to the announcement.

It also wants to "unlock the value potential of professional cycling, elevate the product to better serve a global fan base, and address the need for a more sustainable economic model in professional road cycling and the broadening of its global reach".

The company is registered in the UK and is essentially the same entity as One Cycling, with government files showing the name was changed to Collective Cycling Group on June 2, 2026.

Soon after, ownership of the project changed hands, with Visma-Lease a Bike team boss Richard Plugge standing down both as a 'director' and 'a person with significant control', and replaced in both cases by Oliver Ciesla, a sports marketing executive who previously worked in motorsport.

"This broad and inclusive initiative by so many teams represents a significant milestone in the long and proud history of the sport," Ciesla said.

"Teams carry much of the sporting and financial risk in professional cycling, while many of the sport’s commercial opportunities remain fragmented. The UCI reform process creates a first opportunity to address these challenges together.

"Through a closer cooperation with organisers, the UCI and other stakeholders, teams can create products that none could offer alone, enhancing the experience of fans worldwide, increasing the sport’s visibility, and contributing to a sustainable economic model."

It was not stated in the launch announcement which 24 teams have signed up to form the Collective Cycling Group.

Some teams have since publicly shared the announcement, indicating they are on board. Those teams include EF Education, which has men’s and women’s WorldTour squads, Canyon-SRAM, and Pinarello-Q36.5.

Given Richard Plugge’s prominent role in One Cycling and the push for reform more generally, it can reasonably be assumed that Visma-Lease a Bike are part of the project.

According to , 13 of the 18 men’s WorldTour teams have signed up. The five absentees were said to be UAE Team Emirates-XRG, Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe, Netcompany-Ineos, Jayco-AlUla, and Groupama-FDJ United.

Revamping pro cycling's business model has been a decades-long ambition for many of the stakeholders of a sport

Tour de France owners Amaury Sport Organisation (ASO) are one of the few to be profiting off the sport.

The UCI's formation of the ProTour (now WorldTour) under Hein Verbruggen could be considered to be one of the first attempts at modernizing pro cycling, although the effort was met with extreme resistance from the ASO.

The WorldTour promised to bring more stability to teams, with three-year guaranteed entry into the biggest races, but the sponsorship model of professional cycling remains on shaky ground.

Teams with billionaire backers and generous budgets dominate the sport, while smaller outfits such as TotalEnergies have had to fight for their lives after sponsors pull out.

Even One Cycling wasn't the first try at a new model: In 2011, the Rothschild financial group were backers of what was then called a 'breakaway league' - the World Series Cycling (WSC), with 14 teams on board.

The Velon group came in 2014, with a more modest ambition to add on-board footage and real-time rider stats to their marketing campaigns. How teams really benefited from being a part of Velon is less concrete, and mainly helps with fan engagement and commercialization.

How the CCG will differ from the previous attempts remain to be seen.

How the new CCG project will be received by the UCI should become more clear after the WorldTour seminar, which runs from December 9-10, 2026.

The topics included calendar and participation, the economic model, fan engagement, safety and integrity.

Some of the ideas floated in the document include shortening Grand Tours to 16 days, budget caps, and joint broadcast rights.
